chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a woman whose husband died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth before four months and ten days had passed. She then married. He ruled that the new husband should keep her, then not propose to her (or finalize the marriage) until the end of the later of the two terms (widowhood or pregnancy). If the woman's guardians wish, they may marry her off, and if they wish, they may keep her. If they keep her, they return his wealth (dowry) to him.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ وَ عَشْرٌ: Four months and ten days (standard Iddah for widowhood)
key_terms.الْأَجَلَيْنِ: The two terms (referring to the waiting period of pregnancy and the waiting period of widowhood)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (Iddah) for a pregnant widow who gives birth early, and how does it affect her subsequent marriage?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the principle of 'ta'addud al-iddah' (accumulation of waiting periods) by ruling that a pregnant widow must observe both the duration of her pregnancy and the standard four-month ten-day period, with the marriage becoming final only after the later of the two concludes. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the woman's guardians' choice to either marry her off or retain her, ensuring financial equity through the return of the dowry if they choose the latter. The hadith underscores the protective legal status of the widow during this transitional phase, balancing her reproductive timeline with traditional mourning observances.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a woman widowed from her husband, and she was pregnant. So she gave birth before the passing of four months and ten (days). So she re-married. So he<sup>asws</sup> judged that he should isolate himself from her, then not propose to her until the passing of the later of the two terms. So if the guardians of the woman so desire to, get her married, and if they so desire to, then restrain her. So if they restrain her, his wealth would be returned to him’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and a number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

’Amir al-Mu’minin issued a judgment in the case of a pregnant widow who gave birth before the end of four months and ten days and married. The judgment said that she must be left alone and no one must propose to her for marriage until the longer of the two periods of time ends; and thereafter if her family wants they can give her in marriage or keep her, but if they choose to keep her they must return his (one who had married her) assets.’”
